chapter: Teddy Wilson, Cafe Society and bebop
title: Knowing Lonnie Johnson
summary: Cheatham met Lonnie Johnson in the 1920s and saw him late in life as a hotel doorman in Nashville; the guitar was then mostly a rhythm instrument.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: But you had heard, I assume you had
Oh, absolutely, yes.
Before that?
I knew Lonnie real well.
You knew Lonnie, personally?
Yes.
What was Lonnie like in those days?
Well --
When did you meet him, in the '20's?
I met Lonnie Johnson about in the '20's, yes.
Huh?
I met him around in the '20's. Yes.
Uh-huh.

I wasn't in his company very often, but I met him and he was a very fine fellow, I thought. Why I never, you know -- then I -- we were friendly, but I was going so much that I never ran into him too much, but I -- the last time I saw Lonnie he was in Nashville, Tennessee, I think he was a doorman there in a hotel or something --
In Nashville, Tennessee?
Uh-huh.
When was that, that must've been -- much later.
That was not too long before he died.
I was surprised when I saw him there. Because --
Because I came across Lonnie in Philadelphia, in 1958, I think it was or '59, he was working as a janitor then. And he got back into the music business, made records and --
Yes.
-- I thought he had stayed in the music business until he died, around '69, or so?
Well he was in Nashville, as doorman at a hotel there, and I don't whether he -- I think he did come back, but things weren't too, didn't go to well for him, you know.
Well, he had some -- so many come-backs, ups and downs.
Yes, yes.
But at that time, in the '20's, when you heard him, there weren't too many guitarists playing that kind of guitar --
That's right.
-- were there?
I think -- guitars -- they weren't too popular at that time.
Uh-huh.
They didn't pay too much attention to guitars, guitar was mostly used as a rhythm instrument at that
time.
Yeah.
Definitely were few. He never had an opportunity, I don't think. That he should've had. He died too early, came along a little too early, I think.
